hook: One of the shortest files you are likely to read: a researcher's mirror reflection that does not quite keep up with him. It is a Safe-class oddity told in roughly a dozen sentences, so every line counts. The small behavioral details in the description are worth holding onto.
whyItMatters: It shows how much a micro-length entry can do with one familiar image and a single update. The containment procedure amounts to asking the researcher to keep reporting, which tells you how harmless the situation seems at the outset. Like many very short files, it relies on the reader to build an entire offscreen situation from a few concrete details.
thingsToNotice: The early details, mistimed movements, glances to one side and heavy sweating, read first as a sight gag and then increasingly like nerves. The update is delivered in exactly the same procedural voice as everything else, with no change in register. That flat closing sentence carries the whole effect, and the joke and the chill arrive together.
